page_convention: 1-based physical PDF pages agree with inspected printed labels

checks: The title, author, arXiv version/date and table of contents agree with the supplied source. The scope is finite geometric lattices, representing simple loopless matroids; extensions to arbitrary matroids and polymatroids are explicitly future directions.

The distinction between irreducible built lattices and irreducible underlying lattices is material: irreducible here means top belongs to the chosen building set. Boolean lattices with a top-containing building set are allowed counterexample arities.
The two advertised Koszul arguments have distinct dependencies. A failure in the Leray definition is not, by itself, a refutation of the separate Groebner/PBW route.

proof_coverage.topic: Lattice, building-set, nesting and Comp preliminaries
checks: For a building set, the maximal building elements below X factor [0,X] under join. In Boolean examples this is verified by pairwise disjoint factors covering X; for the maximal building set the factor is X itself.
Nestedness excludes any antichain of at least two nodes whose join is a building element. Spanning requires all maximal building elements; for irreducible targets it includes top.
Induced building sets on [A,B] consist of the non-bottom A∨G lying below B. Restriction/contraction transitivity is immediate from associativity of join with the bottom omitted.

Comp_A(Y) is the unique maximal original building element with A∨Comp_A(Y)=Y. It is defined only for Y in the induced building set. Its injectivity follows from the join left inverse, and order preservation follows by comparing the new factor in the product decomposition.

A nested node cannot equal the join of its strictly smaller maximal nodes: that would be a forbidden antichain with building-set join. Thus every structural local interval is nontrivial. The rank-zero monoidal unit is not an irreducible arity.

The unique minimal nested node above a fixed nonzero building element follows from the forest/product structure; comparable/equality cases were separated. This supplies the corrected weak-inequality choice in F6.
FY is defined by atom sums and nonnested monomials, with x-generators of degree2. The triangular change h_G=sum_{G'>=G}x_G' is integral and invertible.

The projective elimination of x_top requires top in G; F5 gives an explicit reducible counterexample to the universal quantifier. The normal-basis theorem itself applies more broadly, but its top-degree conclusion must count irreducible factors.

The known FY Groebner basis and wonderful-generator version are external inputs (Theorem2.24/Corollary2.25); their full external proofs were not reconstructed. Their exponent inequalities, degree bounds, and concrete rank1–3 consequences were checked.

For positive rank the Orlik-Solomon derivation delta(e_H)=1 contracts the exterior algebra, and ker(delta)=im(delta) follows by multiplication by one atom. The rank-zero unit is a boundary exception to im=ker; subsequent structural arities have positive rank. No separate core defect is claimed from that unused boundary.
OSproj is generated by e_H-e_H' and has the expected Boolean rank1 value K and Boolean rank2 graded dimensions1,1. These dimensions furnish the strong-monoidality scope check in F5.
Objects decompose according to maximal building factors. Tensor products are Cartesian lattice products with the factor building sets, and the empty product is the rank-zero unit.

Structural nested composition is by Comp, not raw inclusion. Phi changes the iterated source intervals by joining with outer lower endpoints. The opposite direction of the poset map representing a categorical isomorphism was tracked.
Lemma3.13 is already a pointwise Comp/Phi identity on each induced-building element. Its factor/maximality proof occurs before the normal-form theorem and can support F1's repair without circularity.

After the replacement invariant, existence follows by moving isomorphisms to the source, flattening structural composites and sorting factors. Images of source tops recover nodes; join with the local bottom recovers factor maps on building elements; atomicity recovers full lattice isomorphisms.

The proper grading is also directly n(source factors)-n(target factors). It is additive for tensor and composition, equals |S|-1 for an irreducible target, and has degree0 only for canonical isomorphisms. This avoids reliance on an informal presentation claim.
The adjacent comparable/nested-incomparable generator exchanges use the canonical interval identifications. No counterexample to the corrected presentation or Feynman hereditary property was found.
For FY[G], h_K goes to the lower h_K if K<=G, otherwise to upper h_{G∨K}. An atom not below G joins G to an upper atom by semimodularity, so its atom relation is killed.

An antichain relation maps either to zero immediately or to a relation indexed by the maximal image antichain times additional factors. Comparable duplicate images can be discarded in this containment argument. This fills the stated generator check without assuming images remain an antichain.

Comparable structural composites agree by the three cases K<=G1, K<=G2 but not G1, and K not<=G2. For nested-incomparable cuts, the product factorization ensures a building element below their join is below one factor. Naturality follows from preservation of joins and building sets.
F6 concerns only the later explicit FY(S) formula. The elementary maps already define the intended cooperad independently.
Generators in Proposition4.4 are top-degree coefficient functionals in irreducible arities. Rank1 gives a legitimate unit-sized arity and no nontrivial atom-difference relation.

The surjectivity induction isolates a minimal positive-index G0 and an exponent mu(G0); a lower cluster of top rank mu+1 evaluates its power with coefficient1. Joins in the upper factor preserve the remaining normal monomial data, with Comp recovering it. At the boundary mu+1=rank(G0), use the singleton top cluster; if G0=top, evaluate the corresponding pure top power directly.

Over Z, injectivity of a dual map alone does not imply surjectivity. Here the displayed isolation argument can be read as an integral unitriangular coefficient-recovery induction, with coefficient1 and no division. That strengthens the proof to a split injection and supports the asserted integral surjectivity. No torsion counterexample is claimed.

The rank identity sum_G rank[τ_S(G),G]=rank(L) follows by peeling a minimal node and using the product interval identification. It gives the degree bound2(rank(L)-|S|). In top-minus-one degree, the normal monomials have at most one proper positive-exponent node.

The quadratic atom-sum functionals evaluate each such normal monomial to1. In the non-comparable atom case, extend the flat by a basis in the upper interval, apply the wonderful relation and kill the induced-atom h generators. Boundary pure-top monomials agree. The kernel step is explicitly deferred to the Groebner argument.

proof_coverage.topic: Poincare-dual FY operad and affine OS cooperad
checks: The FYPD structural formula multiplies by x_G and pulls upper variables back by Comp. Nonnested relations and atom-sum relations are killed using the product factors/linear relations. Its naturality and structural associativity reduce to the same Comp identity.

The relation with FY duality uses the top-degree Poincare pairing. The source's degree conventions should be read with the usual arity regrading; the text alternates ordinary degree2 generators and half-degree notation. A full independent audit of all implicit suspension conventions is not claimed.

The affine OS structural map sends atoms below G to the lower factor and other atoms to their upper join. For a circuit, either the below-G subset is dependent or contraction makes the other images dependent (possibly repeated), so the circuit boundary vanishes. Tensor signs are those of the exterior algebra.
The affine OS assignment is genuinely monoidal on product lattices because atoms/circuits split by the factors. This does not imply the analogous all-built projective-OS assignment in F5.

proof_coverage.topic: Shuffle category, admissible orders, normal monomials and Groebner basis
checks: Induced atom order is determined by the least original atom in each join fiber. Nested interval induction and Phi preserve this order because taking the least element commutes with the partition of the relevant fibers.

The free-operad/shuffle comparison depends on normal forms and is supported after F1. The monomial order is read as the reverse-prefix atom-word order specified by Lemma5.11, with the empty termination symbol largest; ordinary prefix lexicographic shorthand must not be used in a contradictory way.

On fixed quadratic weight, the order comparison survives replacing a factor by the same context. Interval compatibility follows from least atom lifts, and nested factor products preserve comparisons. General nonhomogeneous/infinite-dimensional extensions were not independently established beyond the manuscript's stated argument.

The elementary geometric-lattice EL property can be seen by greedily taking the smallest atom not below the current flat. A purported increasing chain that delays a smaller available atom must acquire it later with a smaller label, a contradiction. This also gives uniqueness and lexicographic minimality.
F2 corrects the frame condition. Non-top retained nodes have local rank>1; top may have rank1. Removing the other rank1 nodes gives clusters, uniquely grouped under their nearest retained parent.
F7 replaces an unnecessary full-fiber equality by equality of minima. The increasing-label conclusion then survives, and a normal cluster is the corresponding truncated increasing EL chain.

With corrected frames, the exponent bijection is alpha_G=rank(local frame interval)-k_G-1. Proper frame exponents are positive, the top exponent may be0, and rank1 top is precisely the k_top=0 case. This is the missing part of the normal-basis cardinality argument.
Exact B3 maximal-building checks give six normal monomials, matching FY Hilbert dimensions1+4t+t^2. The printed frame restriction yields only three; the corrected restriction gives all six.

proof_coverage.topic: Cubicality, odd cooperads, bar/cobar, Leray and Koszulness
checks: F3 replaces the noncomposable displayed reordering formula. Given corrected normal forms, a factorization is encoded by an ordering of its non-top nested nodes; inserting a node in its current local interval recovers every ordering. Permuting the orderings gives a free symmetric-group action.

The composition-orbit bijection in Definition6.1 should target the degree-n component Hom_n(A,B), not all degrees simultaneously. This is a notation repair attached to the cubical discussion, not an independent theorem counterexample.

The shifted projective OS map has the intended total degree under the stated shift, and its image lies in the projective subspaces by delta^2=0 and the kernel identity at positive rank. The all-built object assignment needs F5. Its odd antichain signs fail in the exact example under standard Koszul symmetry; the qualified convention check is recorded separately.

F4 demonstrates that the projective Leray quotient is not a DGA under the printed all-G differential. The corrected proper-G differential preserves the support ideal and atom-sum ideal and squares to zero. This local correction alone is not a complete proof that every later comparison is a chain/cooperad map.

The affine model can keep e_top with d(e_top)=x_top. It must not be presented as having a projective DGA quotient obtained by killing only e_top. The two-colored module extension uses the top multiplication map and the same corrected category data; no independent full reconstruction of the cited comparison is certified.

The bar/cobar adjunction, counit quasi-isomorphism and general quadratic-dual framework are imported from Kaufmann-Ward/Ward. Finite-dimensional arity/weight duals and consistent suspension conventions are needed when using literal algebraic duals; the FY cases are finite in each relevant arity.

For Proposition6.9, a fixed decorated nested monomial has a finite tree of adjacent nodes. A decomposition into normal blocks is determined by which admissible adjacent edges are contracted. Quadraticity ensures this condition is local. The associated graded bar differential is the signed augmented simplex differential on the admissible-edge set.

If that set is nonempty, choosing one vertex gives a contracting homotopy for the augmented simplex. If empty, only the fully split decoration remains, on the quadratic diagonal. Exact rational matrices for0–5 vertices verify the boundary-square and homology conventions.

In each fixed finite arity/weight component the filtration is bounded, so concentration of the associated-graded homology gives the claimed diagonal conclusion. No separate counterexample to the intended quadratic-GB-implies-Koszul statement was found. The final result remains conditional on the corrected constructions and imported framework.

F8 gives exact boundary counterexamples to the proposed rank-function/building-decomposition axiomatization; those statements belong to the outlook and are not used in the established geometric-lattice Koszul chain.

Restriction of a building decomposition is immediate. The contraction construction and the suggested enlarged Feynman category are exploratory here; no certification of the full future extension is made.

F9 is a definite index error in the displayed polymatroid map, already false in a Boolean matroid special case. Correcting the index restores the earlier matroid formula. The whole polymatroid extension and the externally cited generalized Chow-ring definition are not independently certified.

The join-preserving, atom-preserving map in section7.3 sends each wonderful relation to a target relation or a multiple of one, after keeping the maximal image antichain. Inclusion of a building set and lower-interval examples respect the stated hypotheses. Geometric interpretations via blowdowns/marked-point forgetful maps are external identifications, not newly rederived.
The complete bibliography on pp69–70 was read. The review does not claim independent retrieval or full proof verification of every cited source.

leray_crosscheck.claim: Proper building elements index the odd structural generators and the projective bar differential.
reasoning: Page 58 explicitly defines [G]^odd only for G different from the maximal element. The odd category on page 57 introduces the permutation-sign quotient on chains.

The projective Orlik-Solomon cooperad is the projective algebra shifted by [-1], with its unit in grading 1. The structure map includes delta in one factor, and the source remains the projective subalgebra.
The cobar formula on page 60 explicitly sums over proper G in each factor. The bar formula contracts a degree-one structural generator and uses the corresponding permutation signature.
Consequently a projective bar model has no independent edge generator corresponding to cutting at the global top. This agrees with using exterior generators for proper G only.
The bounded check does not re-prove every odd-cooperad sign relation or all global regradings. The shift convention is preserved rather than silently replaced by an unshifted cooperad.
leray_crosscheck.status: Relevant indexing and differential mechanism checked.

leray_crosscheck.claim: The relation e_top=0 is not stable under the differential printed in Definition 6.4.
reasoning: The source first takes all e_G and all x_G for G in the building set, and adds e_top to the ideal. Page 62 then gives d(e_G)=x_G without excluding top.
A derivation on the free algebra descends to its quotient only if the defining ideal is stable. Here the image of the generator e_top of the ideal is x_top.
COUNTEREXAMPLE01 proves x_top is nonzero in an allowed irreducible built lattice. Thus the problem is a literal failure of well-definedness, not an unverified suspicion or an OCR ambiguity.
leray_crosscheck.status: Confirmed by actual images and an explicit finite example.

leray_crosscheck.claim: The proper-exterior-generator correction defines a DGA.
leray_crosscheck.corrected_definition: B_pr=(Lambda_Q(e_G : G in G\{top}) tensor Q[x_G : G in G])/J, where J is generated by e_S x_T with S union T nonnested, and by sum_{G>=H}x_G for every atom H. Use bidegrees |e_G|=(0,1), |x_G|=(2,0), d of bidegree (2,-1), d e_G=x_G and d x_G=0.
proof: Use graded commutativity for total degree: each e is odd and each x is even. Thus the e generators form an exterior algebra over Q.

For a mixed nonnested generator e_S x_T, applying d replaces one proper e_G by x_G. Every surviving summand has exactly the same underlying support S union T, so it is again a nonnested-ideal element. This remains true if a G was already in T, in which case its x exponent increases.
The atom-linear generators have zero differential because every x is closed.
Hence d(J) is contained in J. Since d^2 is zero on all free generators, the odd derivation has d^2=0 on the free graded algebra and the quotient.
All x variables, especially x_top, are retained. No relation x_top=0 is added.

leray_crosscheck.claim: The corrected model is a sub-DGA of the affine model, not the indicated differential quotient.
proof: Let hatB have all e_G, including z=e_top, with the mixed nonnested and atom-linear relations but without e_top=0. The same support argument makes it a DGA, now with d z=x_top.

Adding top to a set neither creates nor removes a nonnested antichain: top is comparable with every building element. Therefore the defining ideal of hatB is the extension of J, and as graded algebras hatB=B_pr tensor Lambda(z).
The algebra B_pr embeds in hatB and is stable under d. The graded projection q:hatB->B_pr with q(z)=0 exists, but it is not a chain map when x_top is nonzero.

A minimal correction to the manuscript can either write B_pr directly with proper e variables, or regard the e_top=0 quotient only as an underlying graded-algebra presentation and define d on its remaining proper generators. It must not retain the universal formula on the zero class e_top.

leray_crosscheck.claim: The projective comparison remains a chain map; the affine atomic generators must not be confused with projective elements.
leray_crosscheck.assumptions: For the general OS quotient, use the well-defined underlying affine algebra map asserted in the manuscript, phi_aff(e_H)=sum_{G>=H}e_G. The full external proof that this respects all circuit relations is not reconstructed here.
proof: Write eta_H=sum_{G>=H,G!=top} e_G. The atom-linear relation gives d eta_H=-x_top, independently of H.

Let phi_pr=q phi_aff as a graded algebra map, where q is the graded projection of L04. On exterior representatives, the graded Leibniz rule gives d phi_pr(alpha)=-x_top phi_pr(delta alpha), with delta(e_H)=1.
Therefore the restriction to the projective algebra overline{OS}=ker(delta) has zero differential and is a chain map into B_pr.

An individual affine generator e_H is not in ker(delta); its image eta_H is generally not closed. Requiring each eta_H to be closed would incorrectly test an affine map instead of the projective comparison actually used on page 62.

Equivalently, writing every affine image with z on the left gives phi_aff(alpha)=phi_pr(alpha)+z phi_pr(delta alpha). Thus a projective element has no z coefficient and its affine image already lies in the sub-DGA B_pr.
leray_crosscheck.status: Chain compatibility proved; general OS-algebra well-definedness is an explicitly retained input.

leray_crosscheck.claim: A conditional objectwise quasi-isomorphism reduction preserves the distinction from the external Leray theorem.
proof: Assume the lattice has positive rank and choose an atom H0. Put eta=eta_{H0} and v=z+eta. Then d v=x_top-x_top=0.
Changing the odd variable z to v gives an isomorphism of DGAs hatB=B_pr tensor Lambda(v), with d v=0. This uses only d eta=-x_top and graded commutativity.

On the Orlik-Solomon side, delta(e_{H0})=1 and delta^2=0 give OS=overline{OS} tensor Lambda(e_{H0}): every alpha decomposes uniquely as (alpha-e_{H0}delta alpha)+e_{H0}delta alpha, with both coefficients in ker(delta).
Under these decompositions, phi_aff sends e_{H0} to v and sends the projective factor through phi_pr. Thus phi_aff=phi_pr tensor id.
Over Q, taking cohomology commutes with tensoring with the two-dimensional zero-differential exterior algebra. Therefore phi_aff is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism if and only if phi_pr is.

In rank one, the proper exterior set is empty and the atom-linear relation gives x_top=0; the formula reduces to Q and its one-generator exterior extension. A zero-rank unit object, if separately adjoined, is treated directly rather than by choosing a nonexistent atom.
leray_crosscheck.limit: This proves an implication conditional on the affine comparison. It does not prove that the cited affine Leray map is a quasi-isomorphism for all built lattices, and the atom choice is not claimed to give a natural splitting of odd cooperads.
leray_crosscheck.status: Conditional algebraic reduction complete; external quasi-isomorphism not re-proved.

leray_crosscheck.claim: Compatibility with the local bar differential and what remains imported for Corollary 6.6.
reasoning: Page 39 defines FYPD([G]) for proper G by inserting a factor x_G and transporting the remaining variables through the Comp_G rule. Pages 39-40 give the relation checks.

A proper exterior monomial e_{G1}...e_{Gr} has differential sum_i (-1)^{i-1} e_{G1}...omit(e_{Gi})...e_{Gr} x_{Gi}. Its sign is the sign of moving the contracted generator to the position used by the bar differential.

Thus, once the graded nested-set component identification quoted from [5], Proposition 5.1.4, is used, the local contraction operation is precisely the insertion of x_G in FYPD([G]). There is no top contraction in the projective case.

The corrected B_pr has exactly the same underlying bigraded algebra as the manuscript's graded quotient by e_top. Therefore the cited graded vector-space decomposition indexed by spanning S with |S|=d+1 has not been changed by the correction.

The complete graded decomposition, its global odd-cooperad compatibility, the identification of the comparison with the canonical quadratic-dual map, and the external Leray quasi-isomorphism remain inputs for the full Corollary 6.6 argument.

The correction supplies the missing well-defined differential and is consistent with those required local operations. This bounded check does not claim a new proof of all those external and categorical identifications.
leray_crosscheck.status: Local differential compatibility checked; full comparison dependencies explicitly retained.

limitations.topic: Shifted odd OS signs on pp58–59
limitations.detail: Under the standard Koszul braiding and the pointwise displayed maps, B3 with G={a,b,c,top} and alpha=delta(e_c e_b e_a) gives first a then ab=-1⊗1⊗1. First b then ab gives+1⊗1⊗1 before the final swap; swapping two shifted degree1 units gives-1⊗1⊗1, so the composites agree rather than being negatives. Page16 explicitly says that graded commutative means with Koszul signs. The odd-OS target is called graded abelian groups, without a separately specified alternative symmetry. A second native helper independently confirmed the calculation and that ordinary coherent suspension transport does not remove this discrepancy. An ordinary ungraded flip makes the required negative relation hold in this example, but is not a verified repair of the whole structure. This note retains the exact failure under the standard Koszul symmetry as a qualified construction/convention concern for parent integration, without claiming a false final theorem or an unconditional convention-independent counterexample.

The source uses degree2 FY generators, top-degree/half-degree Poincare notation, and implicit arity shifts. A literal M versus M-dual projection in the quadratic-duality summary also needs the usual finite-dual interpretation. These were not counted as additional defects without a fixed global convention and full reconstruction.

The logical phrase 'passing to the dual, injectivity suffices' is not valid over arbitrary Z modules. The coefficient-isolation proof can be strengthened to a split integral injection with diagonal1, so no unsupported torsion objection is made.

The full proofs of the FY basis theorem, the Bibby-Denham-Feichtner Leray quasi-isomorphism, Kaufmann-Ward/Ward bar-cobar and Feynman-category results, the full Hodge package, and geometric arrangement/moduli identifications were not independently retrieved or reproved. Their precise use and local hypotheses were tracked. Lack of external author code or supplements is not treated as a mathematical defect.

F1–F3 and F7 have explicit local proof replacements described above. F4 has a well-defined corrected DGA and closed projective-generator map, but the complete comparison theorem and shifted monoidal/cooperadic signs still require a synchronized reconstruction. No blanket certification of all final claims is made.
Boolean, uniform-matroid and simplex calculations are exact reviewer constructions supporting the stated examples only. They are not claimed to prove the general theorems.

detail: This is a bounded independent cross-check, not a full review of M25-0180.
The exact failure of the differential and the proper-generator DGA repair are proved here. A finite rank-two cohomology check cannot prove the general Leray theorem.
The well-defined affine OS algebra map is retained as the manuscript's stated input; all circuit relations in arbitrary built lattices were not separately reconstructed.
The external Leray quasi-isomorphism is not re-proved. The objectwise splitting only proves a conditional implication from that external affine comparison.

The complete graded nested-set decomposition, global odd-cooperad compatibility, regrading conventions across the entire paper, and identification with the canonical Koszul dual map are not all independently re-established.

The literal DGA failure invalidates that definition and the immediate use of it as written. It does not establish that Corollary 6.6's Koszulness conclusion is false or that other proofs in the paper fail.
No further candidate search is pursued after resolving this assigned issue.
